title: Professional Ethics and Independence
exam_relevance: CRITICAL - Heavily tested on CPA AUD exam. Expect 6-10 questions on ethics and independence. This topic also appears on the REG section. Understanding independence rules, prohibited services, and ethical principles is essential for all CPAs.
learning_objectives: Understand the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct structure: principles, rules, and interpretations
Master the fundamental ethical principles: integrity, objectivity, independence, due care, and scope/nature of services
Comprehend independence requirements: independence in fact vs. appearance, covered members
Identify relationships and services that impair independence
Understand differences in independence rules: AICPA, SEC, PCAOB, GAO (Yellow Book)
Know prohibited non-audit services for attest clients
Apply the conceptual framework for threats and safeguards
Understand confidentiality and other professional responsibilities

introduction.overview: Professional ethics and independence are fundamental to the CPA profession. The AICPA Code of Professional Conduct establishes ethical requirements for CPAs. Independence is particularly critical for attestation engagements (audits, reviews, examinations) because users rely on the CPA's objectivity.
introduction.why_ethics_matter: CPAs have a responsibility to the PUBLIC, not just to clients. Unlike other professionals who serve only their clients, CPAs in public practice must maintain independence and objectivity to serve the public interest. This is what gives credibility to financial statements and attestation reports.

code_structure.principles: Broad philosophical statements about CPA responsibilities (aspirational)
code_structure.interpretations: Guidance on how to apply the rules to specific situations
code_structure.hierarchy: If rule conflicts with principle, rule governs. But principles provide context for interpreting rules.

introduction.exam_importance: Ethics and independence are tested extensively. You must know the independence rules (who must be independent, what impairs independence, prohibited services) and the ethical principles.

six_principles_of_professional_conduct.description: The AICPA Code includes six fundamental principles that represent the profession's objectives and ideals.

principle_1_responsibilities.statement: In carrying out their responsibilities as professionals, members should exercise sensitive professional and moral judgments in all their activities.
principle_1_responsibilities.meaning: CPAs have responsibilities to clients, colleagues, employers, and the PUBLIC. Professional judgment must consider all stakeholders.
principle_1_responsibilities.public_interest: CPAs serve the public interest, not just clients. This distinguishes CPAs from other professionals.

principle_2_public_interest.statement: Members should accept the obligation to act in a way that will serve the public interest, honor the public trust, and demonstrate a commitment to professionalism.
principle_2_public_interest.meaning: The PUBLIC relies on CPAs for objective, unbiased professional services. CPAs must honor this trust.
principle_2_public_interest.importance: This is why independence is so critical - serving the public interest requires objectivity and independence from client influence.

principle_3_integrity.statement: To maintain and broaden public confidence, members should perform all professional responsibilities with the highest sense of integrity.
principle_3_integrity.meaning: Integrity means being honest and candid. CPAs should not subordinate judgment to others, should not knowingly misrepresent facts, should not be associated with misleading information.
principle_3_integrity.exam_context: Integrity violations include knowingly being associated with fraudulent FS, making misleading entries, failing to correct known errors.

principle_4_objectivity_and_independence.statement: A member should maintain objectivity and be free of conflicts of interest in discharging professional responsibilities. A member in public practice should be independent in fact and appearance when providing auditing and other attestation services.
principle_4_objectivity_and_independence.objectivity: Objectivity is an intellectual honesty and impartiality - required for ALL CPAs in ALL services.
principle_4_objectivity_and_independence.independence: Independence is freedom from relationships that impair objectivity - required for ATTEST services (audits, reviews, examinations).
principle_4_objectivity_and_independence.key_distinction: ALL CPAs must be OBJECTIVE. Only CPAs performing ATTEST services must be INDEPENDENT.
principle_4_objectivity_and_independence.exam_emphasis: This is the most tested principle. Know the difference between objectivity (all services) and independence (attest only).

principle_5_due_care.statement: A member should observe the profession's technical and ethical standards, strive continually to improve competence and quality of services, and discharge professional responsibility to the best of the member's ability.
principle_5_due_care.meaning: CPAs must be competent, maintain competence through continuing education, and plan/supervise engagements adequately.
components: Sufficient relevant data to support conclusions

principle_6_scope_and_nature_of_services.statement: A member in public practice should observe the Principles of Professional Conduct in determining the scope and nature of services to be provided.
principle_6_scope_and_nature_of_services.meaning: CPAs should consider whether services are consistent with professional obligations. Some services may be inappropriate even if not explicitly prohibited.
considerations: Is there a conflict of interest?
Does the service impair independence for attest services?
Is the CPA competent to perform the service?

independence_fundamental_concepts.description: Independence is the cornerstone of the attest function. Without independence, users cannot rely on the CPA's opinion.

independence_in_fact.definition: A state of mind that permits performing an attest service without being affected by influences that compromise professional judgment, allowing an individual to act with integrity and exercise objectivity and professional skepticism.
independence_in_fact.essence: Actually being independent - having no biases or conflicts
independence_in_fact.problem: Cannot be observed or measured - it's in the CPA's mind

independence_in_appearance.definition: Avoidance of circumstances that would cause a reasonable and informed third party to conclude that the integrity, objectivity, or professional skepticism of a firm or member has been compromised.
independence_in_appearance.essence: APPEARING independent to outsiders - avoiding relationships that create the perception of lack of independence
independence_in_appearance.importance: Even if CPA is actually independent (in fact), if circumstances create appearance of lack of independence, users won't trust the opinion.
independence_in_appearance.example: CPA's spouse owns stock in audit client. Even if CPA can actually be objective (independence in fact), the appearance is that CPA lacks independence. User wouldn't trust the audit.

independence_in_fact_vs_appearance.both_required: CPAs must be independent in BOTH fact AND appearance. Independence in fact alone is insufficient - must also avoid appearance issues.
independence_in_fact_vs_appearance.exam_focus: Most independence questions test appearance. If question asks 'does this impair independence?' - consider whether a reasonable observer would question the CPA's objectivity.

not_required: Compilations (SSARS) - but must disclose if not independent
Agreed-upon procedures (SSAE) - but must disclose if not independent
Consulting services - independence not required (but must maintain objectivity)
when_independence_is_required.exam_tip: If question asks about independence requirement, first determine if it's an attest service providing assurance. Audits and reviews require independence. Compilations and AUP do not.

covered_members.description: Not everyone at the CPA firm must be independent - only 'covered members' must be independent.
who_are_covered_members: 1. Individual on the attest engagement team (anyone who performs attest procedures or reviews work)
2. Individual in a position to influence the attest engagement (partner who supervises engagement partner, quality control reviewers, national office consultants who provide substantial consultation)
3. Partner or manager in the same office as the lead attest engagement partner
5. An entity controlled by any of the above (if material to controlling person)
covered_members.who_is_NOT_a_covered_member: Partners in other offices (unless in position to influence), staff not on engagement team, administrative staff, IT specialists (unless on engagement team)
covered_members.immediate_family_of_covered_members: Spouse, spousal equivalent, and dependents of a covered member are subject to same independence rules as the covered member
covered_members.close_relatives: Close relatives (parent, sibling, non-dependent child) are subject to SOME independence restrictions but not all
covered_members.exam_importance: Know who is a covered member. Many questions ask: 'Partner in Chicago office owns stock in client audited by NY office - is independence impaired?' Answer depends on whether same office or position to influence.

relationships_impairing_independence.description: Certain relationships and interests automatically impair independence for covered members and their immediate family.

direct_financial_interest.definition: Ownership of ANY amount, no matter how small, in a client
direct_financial_interest.rule: Direct financial interest ALWAYS impairs independence, regardless of materiality
examples: Covered member owns 10 shares of audit client stock - impairs independence
Covered member's spouse owns 1 share - impairs independence
Covered member's dependent child owns any amount - impairs independence
direct_financial_interest.exam_emphasis: ANY direct financial interest impairs independence - even $1. Don't need to consider materiality.
direct_financial_interest.exception: Investment in mutual fund that holds client stock is NOT a direct financial interest (it's indirect)

indirect_financial_interest.definition: Ownership through an intermediary (mutual fund, trust, partnership) where the CPA doesn't control investment decisions
indirect_financial_interest.rule: Indirect financial interest impairs independence ONLY if material to the covered member
examples: Covered member owns shares in a mutual fund that owns client stock - indirect interest
CPA is beneficiary of trust that owns client stock but CPA doesn't control trust - indirect interest
indirect_financial_interest.materiality_test: Material to the COVERED MEMBER (not to the client). Consider covered member's net worth.
indirect_financial_interest.exam_scenario: CPA owns $100,000 in mutual fund. Fund owns $5 million of audit client stock. Is independence impaired? Answer: Only if $100,000 is material to CPA's net worth (probably yes unless CPA is very wealthy). The $5M is irrelevant.

permitted_investments.diversified_mutual_fund: Ownership in diversified mutual fund is indirect interest - only impairs if material
permitted_investments.insurance_policy: Cash surrender value of insurance policy is indirect interest
permitted_investments.retirement_plan: Investment through 401(k) or IRA is indirect interest

loans.grandfathered_loans: Loans obtained under normal lending terms BEFORE client became an attest client are permitted if kept current (grandfathered)
loans.home_mortgages: Home mortgages from financial institution client are permitted if obtained under normal lending terms
loans.immaterial_loans: Immaterial loans obtained under normal lending terms from non-financial institution client may be permitted
loans.prohibited_loans: Other loans to/from client impair independence

member_employed_by_client.rule: If covered member (or immediate family) is employed by client in key position, independence is impaired
member_employed_by_client.key_position: Director, officer, employee in accounting/financial reporting role, employee who can exert significant influence over operating/financial policies
member_employed_by_client.example: Covered member's spouse is CFO of audit client - impairs independence
member_employed_by_client.non_key_position: If immediate family member has non-key position (e.g., secretary, janitor), may not impair independence

former_partner_employed_by_client.rule: If FORMER partner/professional employee of the CPA firm is now employed by client in key position, independence is impaired UNLESS: (1) Relationship with firm is completely severed (no continuing payments except for vested benefits), (2) Former partner does not influence firm, (3) Former partner is not in a position to influence attest engagement
former_partner_employed_by_client.exam_scenario: Former audit partner joins client as CFO. Independence impaired UNLESS all continuing payments from firm cease (except vested retirement).

close_relative_employed_by_client.rule: Close relative (parent, sibling, non-dependent child) employed by client in key position impairs independence UNLESS: (1) Covered member is not in position to influence attest engagement, OR (2) Relative is not in position to exert significant influence over client's operating/financial policies

business_relationships.joint_ventures: Material joint venture with client impairs independence
business_relationships.limited_partnerships: General partner interest in partnership that is client impairs independence. Limited partner interest is a financial interest (direct or indirect depending on circumstances).
business_relationships.consignment_arrangements: Material consignment arrangement with client impairs independence

unpaid_fees.rule: Unpaid fees for prior services that become past due create a financial interest that may impair independence
unpaid_fees.generally: If fees from prior year are still unpaid when current year report is issued, independence is impaired (in effect, a loan to the client)
unpaid_fees.exam_note: Must collect prior year fees before issuing current year report

prohibited_non_audit_services.description: When performing attest services for a client, certain non-audit services AUTOMATICALLY impair independence if provided to the same client. These are called 'prohibited services.'
prohibited_non_audit_services.general_principle: If a non-audit service places the CPA in position of being part of management or auditing their own work, independence is impaired.

management_participation.rule: CPA cannot perform management functions or make management decisions for attest client
examples_of_management_functions: Supervising client employees in performance of normal duties
management_participation.what_is_allowed: CPA CAN provide recommendations and advice. CPA CANNOT make the decision for management.
management_participation.exam_distinction: Recommending accounting policy = allowed. Deciding which policy client will use = prohibited.

bookkeeping_accounting_services.generally_prohibited: Bookkeeping services generally impair independence for public companies (SEC clients)
bookkeeping_accounting_services.allowed_for_non_sec_if: For non-SEC clients, bookkeeping is allowed ONLY if: (1) CPA does not make management decisions, (2) Client takes responsibility for FS, (3) Services are NOT extensive (client maintains books and prepares source documents)
bookkeeping_accounting_services.exam_context: If client is SEC registrant, bookkeeping impairs independence. If non-SEC client, allowed if limited and client takes responsibility.

certain_tax_services.generally_allowed: Tax compliance and planning services generally do NOT impair independence
certain_tax_services.prohibited: Representing client in tax court or acting as stock transfer agent impairs independence for SEC clients
certain_tax_services.contingent_fees: Contingent fee tax services impair independence

internal_audit_outsourcing.rule: Providing internal audit services can impair independence if CPA performs management functions
internal_audit_outsourcing.allowed_if: CPA provides assistance to internal audit function but management takes responsibility and makes all decisions
internal_audit_outsourcing.prohibited: CPA cannot BE the internal audit function (management role)

valuation_services.generally_allowed: Valuation services allowed if results are not material to FS and CPA does not make management judgments
valuation_services.prohibited: Material valuations where CPA exercises significant judgment impair independence (auditing own work)
valuation_services.exam_note: Immaterial valuations generally OK. Material valuations that are subjective = impaired.

actuarial_services.rule: Similar to valuation - allowed if immaterial or not subjective, prohibited if material and subjective

it_services.designing_implementing_financial_systems: Designing or implementing financial information systems that generate information for FS generally impairs independence (auditing own work)
it_services.allowed: Assessing computer systems, recommending system improvements, installing off-the-shelf software with no modifications

appraisal_valuation_fairness_opinions.rule: Providing fairness opinions or appraisals for transactions impairs independence if material and subjective

legal_services.general_counsel: Serving as general counsel impairs independence (management function)
legal_services.specific_legal_services: Representing client in litigation, drafting legal documents for material transactions may impair independence

executive_search.rule: Recruiting for management or board positions impairs independence (hiring is management function)
executive_search.allowed: Can assist with recruiting for non-management positions if client makes all decisions

investment_banking.rule: Investment advisory or banking services (arranging financing, underwriting) impair independence

prohibited_non_audit_services.exam_strategy: If a service involves making management decisions or creates situation where CPA audits own work, it impairs independence. Recommendations and advice are OK. Decisions are not.

independence_rules_by_regulator.description: Different regulatory bodies have different independence rules. CPAs must comply with the most restrictive rules applicable.

aicpa_rules.applies_to: All AICPA members performing attest services
aicpa_rules.coverage: Covered in detail above - financial interests, employment, prohibited services, etc.
aicpa_rules.interpretations: AICPA provides detailed interpretations and guidance

sec_independence_rules.generally_more_restrictive: SEC rules are generally MORE restrictive than AICPA rules

key_differences.bookkeeping: Generally prohibited for SEC clients (more restrictive than AICPA)
key_differences.prohibited_services: Longer list of prohibited services than AICPA
key_differences.audit_partner_rotation: REQUIRED - lead partner must rotate off after 5 years, concurring partner after 5 years. Cannot return for 5 years (cooling-off period).
key_differences.pre_approval: Audit committee must PRE-APPROVE all audit and permitted non-audit services
key_differences.financial_relationships: Similar to AICPA but some additional restrictions

sec_independence_rules.exam_focus: Know that SEC rules are more restrictive. Partner rotation, audit committee pre-approval, and bookkeeping prohibition are key differences.

pcaob_rules.applies_to: Audits of public companies registered with SEC
pcaob_rules.similar_to_sec: PCAOB independence rules are similar to SEC rules
pcaob_rules.additional_requirements: PCAOB has additional requirements regarding communication and documentation

gao_yellow_book_independence.applies_to: Government audits and audits of entities receiving government funds

key_differences.broader_scope: Independence requirements apply to broader range of professional services, not just attest
key_differences.personal_impairments: Specifically lists personal impairments: preconceived ideas, bias, personal relationships that compromise objectivity
key_differences.organizational_impairments: Restrictions on audit firm providing certain non-audit services
key_differences.non_audit_services: MORE restrictive than AICPA regarding non-audit services for government audit clients

gao_yellow_book_independence.exam_note: Yellow Book independence is MORE restrictive than AICPA rules. Most government audit questions are on REG exam, but concept appears on AUD.

dol_independence_rules.applies_to: Audits of employee benefit plans subject to ERISA
dol_independence_rules.rule: Department of Labor has specific independence rules for benefit plan audits
dol_independence_rules.exam_relevance: Rarely tested - just know the concept exists

independence_rules_by_regulator.exam_strategy: AICPA rules are the baseline. SEC/PCAOB rules are more restrictive. GAO (Yellow Book) rules are even more restrictive. When question asks about public company audit, consider SEC rules. Government audit, consider GAO rules.

conceptual_framework_threats_and_safegua.description: The AICPA Code uses a 'conceptual framework' approach. If a specific rule doesn't address a situation, the CPA evaluates threats to independence and applies safeguards.

adverse_interest_threat.description: CPA and client have opposing interests

advocacy_threat.description: CPA promotes client's position to point that objectivity is compromised
advocacy_threat.examples: CPA acts as advocate in litigation, promotes client's securities

familiarity_threat.description: Close relationship with client causes CPA to become too sympathetic to client's interests
familiarity_threat.examples: Long association with client, family member employed by client, former partner now at client

management_participation_threat.description: CPA performs management functions or makes management decisions
management_participation_threat.examples: CPA authorizes transactions, supervises employees, sets policies

self_interest_threat.description: CPA has financial or other interest that could inappropriately influence judgment
self_interest_threat.examples: Direct financial interest in client, excessive fees from one client, contingent fees

self_review_threat.description: CPA reviews own work or work of firm
self_review_threat.examples: Auditing financial statements prepared by CPA's firm, auditing systems designed by firm

undue_influence_threat.description: Client attempts to coerce or exercise excessive influence over CPA
undue_influence_threat.examples: Threat to replace CPA, pressure to reduce audit work, intimidation

safeguards.description: Actions that eliminate or reduce threats to an acceptable level
safeguards_in_work_environment: Involvement of additional CPAs for consultation
Reporting structure that separates attest function from other services
safeguards_specific_to_engagement: Involving another firm to perform part of engagement
Using professionals not otherwise associated with attest engagement to review work

applying_framework.step_3: Identify and apply safeguards to eliminate or reduce threats to acceptable level
applying_framework.step_4: If no safeguards can reduce threat, decline or withdraw from engagement

conceptual_framework_threats_and_safegua.exam_application: If question describes unusual situation not covered by specific rule, think about which threat exists and whether safeguards could address it.

confidentiality.rule: Member shall not disclose confidential client information without specific client consent
exceptions_permitted_disclosure: Disclosure required by court order or subpoena (legal/regulatory requirement)
Peer review (other CPAs reviewing firm's work)
Disclosure to comply with professional standards (e.g., communicating fraud to successor auditor when required)
confidentiality.exam_scenario: CPA discovers fraud at client. Can CPA report to authorities without client consent? Generally NO (unless specific legal requirement). Must withdraw from engagement if client doesn't address.
confidentiality.key_point: Confidentiality continues even after professional relationship ends

acts_discreditable.rule: Member shall not commit acts discreditable to the profession
examples: Failure to follow government audit standards when required
Negligence in preparation of FS or tax returns
Failure to file own tax return or pay taxes
Solicitation or disclosure of CPA exam questions/answers
Failure to comply with rules and regulations of government bodies
Making false, misleading, or deceptive claims about services
acts_discreditable.exam_note: Discreditable acts bring disrepute to the profession

advertising_and_solicitation.general_rule: Advertising and solicitation are ALLOWED as long as not false, misleading, or deceptive
advertising_and_solicitation.allowed: Factual advertising about services, qualifications, fees. Can solicit clients.
advertising_and_solicitation.exam_note: Used to be very restrictive - now very permissive. Almost all advertising allowed as long as truthful.

commissions_and_referral_fees.commission_definition: Compensation for recommending a product or service
commissions_and_referral_fees.referral_fee_definition: Compensation for recommending another CPA's services

rules.attest_clients: PROHIBITED to receive commission or referral fee from client for whom CPA performs attest services (impairs independence)
rules.non_attest_clients: ALLOWED to receive commission or referral fee ONLY IF disclosed to client
rules.paying_referral_fee: ALLOWED to pay referral fee to obtain client (even attest client) as long as disclosed

commissions_and_referral_fees.exam_scenario: CPA receives commission for selling accounting software to audit client - PROHIBITED (impairs independence). Same commission from non-attest tax client - ALLOWED if disclosed.

contingent_fees.definition: Fee that depends on finding or result (e.g., percentage of tax refund, fee if loan approved)
prohibited_for: Tax returns and claims for refunds for current or prior year if CPA also performs attest services for client
contingent_fees.allowed_for: Non-attest clients (tax, consulting, etc.) and some tax services
contingent_fees.exam_distinction: Contingent fees OK for consulting. NOT OK for attest clients or tax work for attest clients.

form_of_organization.general_rule: CPAs can practice in any form of organization (sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, LLC) as long as: (1) Complies with state law, (2) Owners are CPAs (though some non-CPA ownership allowed), (3) CPA remains personally responsible for attest work
form_of_organization.ownership: Majority ownership must be CPAs, but some states allow non-CPA ownership (usually up to 49%)
form_of_organization.exam_note: CPAs can incorporate or form LLCs - not limited to partnerships

practice_problems.question:
For each scenario, determine whether independence is impaired:

Scenario A: John Smith, CPA, is the engagement partner on the audit of ABC Company. John's spouse owns 100 shares of ABC Company stock (valued at $2,500). John and his spouse's combined net worth is $1.5 million.

Scenario B: Sarah Jones, CPA, is a partner in the Chicago office of a CPA firm. The firm's New York office audits XYZ Company. Sarah is not involved in the audit and has no influence over it. Sarah owns 50 shares of XYZ Company stock.

Scenario C: Mike Chen, CPA, performs the annual review of DEF Company's financial statements. Mike's non-dependent adult son is the CFO of DEF Company.

Scenario D: Lisa Brown, CPA, performs the audit of GHI Company. Lisa owns shares in a mutual fund that owns GHI Company stock. The mutual fund investment represents 5% of Lisa's net worth.

reasoning.covered_member: John is the engagement partner - he is a covered member
reasoning.immediate_family: John's spouse is immediate family - subject to same independence rules as John
reasoning.direct_financial_interest: Spouse's stock ownership is a DIRECT financial interest in the audit client
reasoning.materiality_irrelevant: Direct financial interest impairs independence regardless of materiality. The $2,500 amount and the fact that it's only 0.17% of net worth are irrelevant.
reasoning.conclusion: ANY direct financial interest by covered member or immediate family impairs independence

scenario_A.exam_principle: Direct financial interest ALWAYS impairs independence, no matter how small. Don't analyze materiality for direct interests.

reasoning.covered_member_analysis: Sarah is a partner, but is she a COVERED MEMBER for the XYZ audit? Covered members include: (1) engagement team members, (2) those who can influence engagement, (3) partners in SAME OFFICE as lead engagement partner.
reasoning.different_office: Sarah is in Chicago office, engagement is run from New York office - DIFFERENT offices
reasoning.no_influence: Facts state Sarah is not involved and has no influence
reasoning.conclusion: Sarah is NOT a covered member for the XYZ audit because she's in a different office and has no influence
reasoning.therefore: Independence is NOT impaired (Sarah is not a covered member, so her stock ownership doesn't matter)

scenario_B.exam_principle: Partners in DIFFERENT offices who do not influence the engagement are NOT covered members. Their financial interests don't impair independence.
scenario_B.caveat: If Sarah COULD influence the engagement (e.g., she's on quality control committee), then she would be a covered member and independence would be impaired.

reasoning.covered_member: Mike performs the review - he is a covered member
reasoning.close_relative: Non-dependent adult son is a 'close relative' (not immediate family)
reasoning.key_position: CFO is definitely a key position at the client
reasoning.close_relative_rule: Close relative in key position at client impairs independence UNLESS: (1) covered member not in position to influence engagement, OR (2) relative not in position to influence client's financial policies
reasoning.application: Mike PERFORMS the review (definitely influences it), and son is CFO (definitely influences financial policies)
reasoning.conclusion: Independence is impaired - close relative in key position and neither exception applies

scenario_C.exam_principle: Close relatives (parents, siblings, non-dependent children) in key positions at client generally impair independence unless specific exceptions apply.

reasoning.covered_member: Lisa performs the audit - she is a covered member
reasoning.indirect_financial_interest: Mutual fund ownership is an INDIRECT financial interest (not direct - Lisa doesn't directly own the GHI stock)
reasoning.materiality_test: Indirect financial interest impairs independence ONLY if material to the covered member
reasoning.materiality_analysis: The mutual fund represents 5% of Lisa's net worth - this is likely MATERIAL
reasoning.conclusion: 5% is material to most people's net worth, so independence is likely impaired

scenario_D.exam_principle: Indirect financial interests impair independence only if MATERIAL to the covered member. 5% of net worth is generally considered material.
scenario_D.note: If the mutual fund were only 0.5% of net worth, probably immaterial and wouldn't impair independence.

practice_problems.question:
ABC Company is an audit client. For each service below, determine whether providing the service to ABC would impair independence:

Service A: Preparing ABC's tax return
Service B: Recommending accounting software for ABC to purchase
Service C: Installing and customizing the accounting software that generates ABC's financial statement information
Service D: Providing bookkeeping services where ABC's employees maintain all the books and prepare source documents, and the CPA only helps with adjusting entries
Service E: Representing ABC in an IRS audit
Service F: Recruiting and interviewing candidates for ABC's CFO position, with ABC making the final hiring decision

service_A_tax_return.reasoning: Tax compliance services generally do NOT impair independence. Preparing tax returns is a traditional CPA service that doesn't involve making management decisions or auditing own work.
service_A_tax_return.exam_principle: Tax return preparation is allowed for audit clients

service_B_recommending_software.reasoning: Providing recommendations and advice does not impair independence. The CPA is recommending, not deciding. Management makes the decision.
service_B_recommending_software.exam_principle: Recommendations are OK. Decisions are not.

reasoning.self_review_threat: Installing and customizing accounting software that generates financial statement information creates a self-review threat - the auditor would be auditing FS generated by a system the auditor designed/implemented
reasoning.rule: Designing or implementing financial information systems impairs independence
reasoning.distinction: Installing off-the-shelf software with NO customization might be OK. But customizing the system that generates FS data = impaired.

service_C_installing_customizing_softwar.exam_principle: Designing/implementing financial systems = auditing own work = impaired independence

service_D_bookkeeping.independence: NOT IMPAIRED (for non-SEC client) or IMPAIRED (for SEC client)

reasoning.general_rule: Bookkeeping services can impair independence (auditing own work)
reasoning.non_sec_exception: For NON-SEC clients, limited bookkeeping is allowed IF: (1) client maintains books and prepares source documents, (2) client takes responsibility for FS, (3) services are not extensive
reasoning.application: The facts state ABC's employees maintain books and prepare source documents, and CPA only helps with adjusting entries - this meets the exception
reasoning.conclusion: If ABC is non-SEC client, independence NOT impaired. If ABC is SEC registrant, independence IS impaired (SEC generally prohibits bookkeeping).

service_D_bookkeeping.exam_tip: For bookkeeping questions, check if client is SEC registrant. SEC rules are more restrictive.

service_E_irs_representation.reasoning: Representing client before IRS is generally allowed. The CPA is advocating for the client's position on tax matters, which is expected. This doesn't create independence issues for financial statement audit.
service_E_irs_representation.exception: For SEC clients, representation in certain tax matters may impair independence
service_E_irs_representation.exam_principle: Tax representation generally OK for audit clients (unless SEC client with restrictions)

reasoning.management_function: Recruiting for executive positions (like CFO) is a management function. Hiring employees is management's responsibility.
reasoning.even_if_client_decides: Even though ABC makes the final decision, the CPA's involvement in recruiting and interviewing for a key management position (CFO) impairs independence
reasoning.rule: Executive search for management positions impairs independence

service_F_executive_search.exam_principle: Recruiting for management/board positions = management function = impaired independence. Can help recruit for non-management positions if client makes all decisions.

tip_1_direct_vs_indirect_financial_inter.description: This is the most tested independence concept
tip_1_direct_vs_indirect_financial_inter.direct: ANY amount impairs independence - don't consider materiality
tip_1_direct_vs_indirect_financial_inter.exam_strategy: First determine if direct or indirect. If direct, it impairs (done). If indirect, assess materiality to the covered member.

tip_2_covered_members.covered_members: Engagement team, those who can influence engagement, partners in same office
tip_2_covered_members.not_covered: Partners in different offices (unless can influence), staff not on engagement
tip_2_covered_members.exam_trap: Partner owns stock in client audited by different office - independence NOT impaired (different office, no influence)

tip_3_immediate_family_vs_close_relative.immediate_family: Spouse, spousal equivalent, dependents - same rules as covered member
tip_3_immediate_family_vs_close_relative.close_relatives: Parents, siblings, non-dependent children - limited restrictions
tip_3_immediate_family_vs_close_relative.exam_question: Covered member's spouse in key position at client = impaired. Covered member's non-dependent child in key position = may be impaired depending on circumstances.

tip_4_prohibited_services.general_rule: Management functions and auditing own work impair independence
tip_4_prohibited_services.examples: Designing financial systems, making management decisions, extensive bookkeeping (especially SEC clients), executive search for management
tip_4_prohibited_services.allowed: Recommendations, tax services (generally), limited bookkeeping (non-SEC), advisory services where client decides
tip_4_prohibited_services.exam_strategy: If service involves CPA making decision or CPA later auditing own work, it impairs independence

tip_5_sec_vs_aicpa_rules.sec_differences: Bookkeeping generally prohibited, partner rotation required, audit committee pre-approval required, longer list of prohibited services
tip_5_sec_vs_aicpa_rules.exam_tip: If question mentions public company or SEC registrant, think about SEC rules (more restrictive)

tip_6_independence_required_when.description: Independence only required for attest services providing assurance
tip_6_independence_required_when.not_required: Compilations, AUP, tax, consulting (but must disclose if not independent for compilations/AUP)
tip_6_independence_required_when.exam_question: CPA owns stock in client. Can CPA provide tax services? YES (independence not required for tax). Can CPA audit? NO (independence required).

tip_7_confidentiality_exceptions.description: Confidentiality is the rule, but there are exceptions
tip_7_confidentiality_exceptions.generally_confidential: Cannot disclose client information without consent
tip_7_confidentiality_exceptions.exceptions: Court order/subpoena, peer review, ethics investigation, required by professional standards, authorized by client
tip_7_confidentiality_exceptions.exam_scenario: CPA discovers fraud. Can CPA report to SEC without client consent? Generally NO (confidentiality). Must withdraw if client won't address.

tip_8_commissions_and_contingent_fees.description: Different rules for attest vs. non-attest clients
tip_8_commissions_and_contingent_fees.attest_clients: PROHIBITED to receive commissions or contingent fees (impairs independence)
tip_8_commissions_and_contingent_fees.non_attest_clients: ALLOWED to receive commissions or contingent fees if DISCLOSED
tip_8_commissions_and_contingent_fees.exam_question: CPA receives commission for selling software to audit client? PROHIBITED. To tax-only client? ALLOWED if disclosed.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: CPA or family member owns stock in client - is independence impaired?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Determine if covered member, if immediate family or close relative, if direct or indirect interest, assess materiality if indirect

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Can CPA provide [specific service] to audit client?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Does service involve management decision or audit own work? If yes, impaired. If just recommendation, OK.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Partner in Office A owns stock in client audited by Office B
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Different offices, no influence = not covered member = independence not impaired

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Former partner now works for client
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Independence impaired UNLESS all payments cease (except vested benefits) and former partner doesn't influence firm or engagement
If prior year fees still unpaid when current year report issued, impairs independence (in effect, a loan)

memorization_aids.direct_financial_interest: Direct = Any amount impairs (no materiality test)
memorization_aids.immediate_family: Spouse and dependents = same rules as covered member
memorization_aids.prohibited_services_mnemonic: Management functions and Auditing own work = Impaired (MAI)
memorization_aids.sec_differences: SEC = More Strict (bookkeeping prohibited, rotation required, pre-approval required)

key_concepts: Independence required for attest services (audits, reviews, examinations) but not for compilations, AUP, tax, or consulting
Must be independent in BOTH fact and appearance
Covered members: engagement team, those who can influence engagement, partners in same office
Direct financial interest ALWAYS impairs independence (any amount). Indirect only if material.
Immediate family (spouse, dependents) subject to same rules as covered member
Services involving management decisions or auditing own work impair independence
SEC rules more restrictive than AICPA rules (bookkeeping prohibited, rotation, pre-approval)
Six principles: Responsibilities, Public Interest, Integrity, Objectivity/Independence, Due Care, Scope of Services
Confidentiality required with exceptions: court order, peer review, ethics investigation, required by standards
Commissions and contingent fees prohibited for attest clients
critical_for_exam: Direct vs. indirect financial interests and materiality
Who is a covered member (engagement team, influencers, same office partners)
Prohibited services (management functions, auditing own work)
When independence is required (attest with assurance) vs. not (compilations, AUP, tax, consulting)
common_mistakes: Thinking materiality matters for direct financial interests - it doesn't (any amount impairs)
Thinking partners in different offices are covered members - they're not (unless can influence)
Thinking all services to audit clients impair independence - only management functions and auditing own work
Forgetting SEC rules are more restrictive than AICPA
Thinking independence required for all CPA services - only for attest with assurance
Confusing immediate family (spouse, dependents) with close relatives (parents, siblings, non-dependent children)

primary_standards: AICPA Code of Professional Conduct - ET Section 1.200 (Independence)
AICPA Code of Professional Conduct - ET Section 1.100 (Integrity and Objectivity)
AICPA Code of Professional Conduct - ET Section 0.300 (Principles)
GAO Yellow Book (Government Auditing Standards) - Independence
